blacklistabilityReview.evidence: At fixed 2026-07-15 blocks Ethereum 25534997, Base 48646186, Worldchain 32373046, BSC 110049753, Polygon 90251163, and Gnosis 47208124, every tracked WCOP proxy resolved to 0x6f6206fac28d9f60d221a63aae5fb5c3a9ea6652 and returned paused() = false. On each route, 0x466c02e2cc67b81a696af5afdb61605c41fe247b held both PAUSER_ROLE and UPGRADER_ROLE. Ethereum, Base, and Worldchain run the verified pausable LatamStable variant, so that EOA can halt all ERC-20 updates; BSC, Polygon, and Gnosis run the verified compliance variant, which additionally exposes blockUser, unblockUser, and setEnforceBlocklist and rejects a blocked sender or receiver in _update when enforcement is enabled. This is an asset-wide direct freeze conclusion from all six tracked routes, but address-specific blocklisting is only asserted for BSC, Polygon, and Gnosis. The V9 transfer review is resolved by the direct pause/blocklist mechanisms, not a permissioning-adapter inference. Ripio's public GitHub organization did not expose a wFIAT/LatamStable Solidity repository, and Archive.org returned no snapshot for the reviewed English wFIAT page; deployed explorer source and fixed RPC evidence remain sufficient. The issuer's March 2026 collateral certification was reviewed as transparency evidence, not as access-control proof.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: wCOP has seven independent native issuance deployments, including Celo, and separate issuer-operated burn/mint transfer machinery. Celo's complete issuance census distinguishes native LimitedMinter issuance from two receipt-authenticated BridgeDeposit transfers; it is not a conserved bridge-only claim. Native Safe and facility powers are recorded in Mint Authority, while bridge-adapter, operator, administration, pause and raiseable-cap powers remain here. Across is a separate liquidity/intent rail.

routes.protocol: Ripio native issuance with issuer-operated burn/mint transfer rail
routes.reviewNote: At Celo block 79288027, verified LatamStable native mint is held by the local 4-of-7 Safe and native LimitedMinter, independently of LimitedMinterBridge. The complete 41-event token history from creation records four mints; all four are authenticated against RPC receipts. Native LimitedMinter issued 100 WCOP on June 5 and 30000000 on September 9 without a source burn. BridgeDeposit fulfilled 999943 and 2999943 WCOP from exact Worldchain/Ethereum burns; pinned totalMintedFrom counters match those transfers, and no Celo WCOP burns are recorded. Net issuance equals current 33999986 WCOP supply. This establishes independent native liabilities plus a transfer rail, not a conserved bridge-only representation. Current native role/upgrade powers are added to Mint Authority and Celo bridge authorities are separately enumerated here. Issuer launch/release disclosures, repository audit material, independent incident-index searches and complete token/facility histories were reviewed; no unexplained Celo issuance, upgrade or fulfillment was identified. Fiat backing is not independently reconciled and signer independence is not inferred.

controls.label: Ripio WCOP LimitedMinterBridge adapter
controls.capDescription: Historical 2026-08-16 reads of the six referenced deployments returned exists=true and dailyMaxMint=1580416570821698384 raw units (1.580416570821698384 WCOP). These observations are not re-dated. The separately reviewed Celo facility now has its own current control record. Administrators can change token registration and daily limits; minters can choose arbitrary recipients.
bypassSurfaces: The issuer EOA held MINTER_ROLE on the Ethereum adapter and can call its arbitrary-recipient mintTo() path without BridgeDeposit burn proof; the token-level issuer MINTER_ROLE remains a separate native issuance surface.

routeChecks.caps: The adapter's wCOP dailyMaxMint was 1.580416570821698384 WCOP at the reviewed reads, and the source permits an administrator to change token registration and daily limits.
routeChecks.trustedPeerOrRemote: BridgeDeposit.depositForBridge() burns source WCOP and an authorized operator fulfills destination minting through LimitedMinterBridge; Ethereum route configurations to Base, Worldchain, BSC, Polygon, Gnosis, and Celo were enabled with a fixed 57 WCOP fee.
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: LimitedMinterBridge is source-verified and non-upgradeable. Its admin surface controls token registration, daily limits, and pause; Ethereum DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE was held by the issuer EOA and Ripio Safe, with no timelock evidenced.
routeChecks.onchainAmountBounds: BridgeDeposit exposes totalBurnedTo/totalMintedFrom accounting and the Worldchain counters were nonzero at the observed Ethereum block, but paired source/destination reconciliation for these six routes was not completed. The issuer EOA's adapter MINTER_ROLE creates a capped arbitrary-recipient bypass of burn proof.

controls.evidence: The historical 2026-08-16 observations of the six referenced deployments are retained. Verified LimitedMinterBridge source defines issuer-operated bridge minting, daily limits, admin-controlled registration, pause and arbitrary recipients. Ethereum role enumeration found the issuer EOA and BridgeDeposit as MINTER holders and EOA/Safe as administrators. Celo is removed from this shared historical observation and receives exact Celo controller records after the R17 pinned native/transfer review; its native mint capabilities remain in Mint Authority.

routeChecks.caps: The Safe's DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE can grant bridge roles and change LimitedMinterBridge token registration and daily limits.
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: At Ethereum block 25770680 the Safe was a 4-of-7 Safe with no enabled modules; the bridge contracts are not governed by a timelock in the reviewed source and the adapter is non-upgradeable.

controls.evidence: At the reviewed Ethereum role enumeration, Ripio Safe 0x2b839174fe62466067c22e2a4c8054071f9d8d68 held DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE on both bridge contracts.
